title: Growth Rate and CAGR Computation from DI
tagline: Year 3 — Total growth, average annual growth and compound annual growth rate from start and end values

introduction.overview: Growth can be measured in three ways. Total growth is the change over the whole period as a percentage of the start. The simple average annual growth divides total growth by the number of years. The compound annual growth rate (CAGR) is the single yearly rate that, applied every year, takes the start value to the end value: CAGR = (end ÷ start)^(1/n) − 1. They differ when the yearly rates vary, and a good analyst knows which one a question asks for.
introduction.placementRelevance: CAGR and growth-rate questions appear in management-oriented DI sets and in finance sections.
introduction.realWorldContext: Investment returns, company revenue and population growth are reported as CAGR.

learningObjectives: Compute total growth as a percentage
Distinguish simple average growth from CAGR
Project a value forward at a given CAGR
Use the rule of 72 for doubling time

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Value after n years at rate r: start × (1 + r)ⁿ. Total growth = (end − start) ÷ start.

coreDefinitions: Simple average growth: total growth ÷ number of years.
CAGR: the constant yearly rate that gives the same end value.
Year-on-year (YoY) growth: change from one year to the next.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Compounding means each year's growth is on the previous year's larger base. CAGR is the one steady rate that does the same job.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For short periods try common rates: 10% for 3 years gives 1.331, 20% gives 1.728, 5% gives 1.1576, 25% gives 1.953. Match the ratio end ÷ start with a known power.

mainNarrative: Investment A grew from 1,000 to 1,331 in three years. Total growth is 331 ÷ 1,000 = 33.1%. Since 1.1³ = 1.331, the CAGR is exactly 10%. The simple average annual growth is 33.1% ÷ 3 = 11.0%, which overstates the true yearly rate.
Investment D grew from 64 to 125. The ratio is 1.953, and (5/4)³ = 125/64, so the CAGR is 25%. Its total growth is 95.3%.
Investment F fell from 1,000 to 729. The ratio is 0.729 = 0.9³, so the CAGR is −10%, and the total decline is 27.1%.

For a series with varying yearly rates, the average of the YoY rates is not the CAGR. With revenue 100, 110, 132, 138.6 and 173.25 the yearly rates are 10%, 20%, 5% and 25% (mean 15%), but CAGR = (1.7325)^(1/4) − 1 ≈ 14.7%.
A rise of 10% followed by a fall of 10% does not return to the start: 100 × 1.1 × 0.9 = 99.

deepDiveAspects.title: CAGR below the mean of YoY rates
deepDiveAspects.content: By compounding, CAGR is less than the arithmetic mean of the yearly rates when the rates vary.

deepDiveAspects.title: Percent up then down
deepDiveAspects.content: Percentage changes do not cancel because each applies to a different base.

solvedExamples.title: Total growth
solvedExamples.question: An investment grows from ₹1,000 thousand to ₹1,331 thousand in 3 years. What is the total growth?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The base is the start value.

solvedExamples.title: CAGR
solvedExamples.question: An investment grows from ₹1,000 thousand to ₹1,331 thousand in 3 years. What is the CAGR?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Compounded for three years it gives 1.331.

solvedExamples.title: Projection
solvedExamples.question: Investment B (₹864 thousand) keeps growing at its CAGR of 20%. What will it be after 2 more years?

shortcutMethods.title: Match the power

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Use a calculator for the root.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Compare end ÷ start with 1.1³, 1.2³, 1.05³, 1.25³ and so on to read off CAGR for short periods.

rulesForApplication: CAGR uses a root, not a division.
Up 10% then down 10% is not zero.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: CAGR must be below the simple average when growth is positive.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Test a candidate CAGR by raising it to the power n.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I compute CAGR for 3 years?
Can I tell it from the simple average?
